summary: Goode Ridge (Chelan County) had L-4 cabs built in 1937 and 1939; the first was blown over a cliff in 1938 and the second removed or destroyed in 1950. An NPS trail now leads toward the ridge.

facts.design: L-4 cab built 1937 (blown over a cliff in 1938); second L-4 cab built 1939
facts.status_note: Second cab removed (register) or destroyed (firelookout.com, Willhite) in 1950; the NPS says the lookout was removed years ago and most of what is left is broken glass among the rocks

access.note: Hiking trail in North Cascades National Park; no camping along the trail; overnight stays need a backcountry permit

visit.trail_note: Five miles one way from the Upper Stehekin Valley Trail; about 4,400 ft of gain; rated strenuous; snowpack can obscure the upper trail well into late July in most years

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (per the register, for the lookout era); the trail is now a National Park Service trail

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 7,400 feet; Willhite gives 6,780 feet for the lookout. The story reports both.
The register says removed in 1950; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1950. The story reports both wordings.
The register lists the U.S. Forest Service for the lookout; the NPS trail page describes the trail today. The story reports each for its own period.

notes_for_editor: Willhite's page is titled 'Goodie Ridge'; the register, firelookout.com and the NPS use 'Goode Ridge', and the record uses Goode. Willhite had not visited the site, so his page describes records, not the site. The NPS page is about the trail. It says the lookout was removed years ago and that most of what remains of the building is scattered glass among the rocks, which the story now reports. The NPS page contains the spelling 'decommisioned', which is quoted as written. The brief's record has no corrections. No staffing information was found in the sources read, so staffing is omitted. The Alpine Guide and NWHikers pages from the search were not read.
